title: Nayanthara and South Indian Stars Bring the Kasavu Saree Back Into the Spotlight for Onam 2026
excerpt: As Kerala's biggest harvest festival peaks with Thiruvonam on August 26, the 'Lady Superstar' and fellow actresses are setting festive fashion benchmarks in the traditional white-and-gold drape.
body:
• Onam 2026 celebrations run from August 16 to 26, with Thiruvonam falling on Wednesday, August 26, marking the festival's grand culmination.
  • Nayanthara's minimalist approach to the Kasavu saree — a classic white drape with thin gold border, paired with traditional jhumkas — has become an enduring style reference for the festival.
  • Designers are introducing contemporary twists for 2026, from pastel accents and Kalamkari prints to pre-draped options and fusion silhouettes, while the iconic cream-and-gold palette holds firm.
  • Nayanthara's film Gold, co-starring Prithviraj Sukumaran and directed by Alphonse Puthren, is set for an Onam season theatrical release.

The Festival and Its Fashion

Kerala's ten-day Onam festival is in full swing, and as always, the Kasavu saree sits at the heart of the celebration's sartorial identity. The traditional off-white or cream handloom cotton drape with its distinctive golden zari border remains the undisputed wardrobe choice for millions of women across South India and the diaspora.

Thiruvonam, the festival's main day, falls on Wednesday, August 26 this year, and the run-up has already seen a flood of celebrity-inspired fashion content on social media. At the center of this conversation, as she often is, stands Nayanthara — the actress known as the Lady Superstar of South Indian cinema, whose approach to the Kasavu has become a benchmark.

Nayanthara's Signature Minimalism

While many celebrities reach for elaborate embellishments and heavy accessories, Nayanthara has consistently gravitated toward restraint. Her Onam looks typically feature a classic white saree with a thin gold border, paired with traditional jhumkas and her hair swept into a sleek bun — simple choices that have made her one of the most referenced style icons for the festival, according to Filmfare.

"Nayanthara likes to keep it simple with her sarees. She's not been seen that often in sparkling fabrics and likes to keep it minimal and eye-catching."

— Filmfare

That minimalism extends beyond just the saree. Whether she's attending an Ambani wedding in an off-white Kanjeevaram with golden threadwork or stepping out in a lilac cotton drape with subtle white motifs, the actress lets the fabric and craftsmanship do the talking. Her choices have influenced a generation of women who see the Kasavu as something more than ceremonial — it's a statement of understated elegance.

The Broader 2026 Trend

Nayanthara is far from alone in championing the Kasavu this season. Kalyani Priyadarshan was recently spotted in a golden-hued tissue silk Kasavu saree with a modern cream spaghetti strap blouse by designer Poornima Indrajith. Keerthy Suresh paired an ivory cotton Kasavu with a bright red sleeveless blouse for dramatic contrast. Anupama Parameswaran went with a traditional cream silk saree and a contrasting puffed-sleeve blouse, while Rashmika Mandanna opted for a nude-coloured tissue silk interpretation with a sophisticated V-neckline.

Designers this year are pushing the boundaries of what the Kasavu can be. Kochi-based designer Revathy Jayan Babu's collection Pooram draws inspiration from Kerala temple festivals, incorporating elephants, muthukuda motifs, and Malayalam lettering into playful prints and pastel washes. Sreejith Jeevan's Pulari collection reimagines Onam dressing through landscape-inspired appliqué textiles in shades of blue, mint, and yellow, moving beyond the familiar white-and-gold.

Onam at the Box Office

The festival season also carries significance for Nayanthara on the professional front. Her film Gold, co-starring Prithviraj Sukumaran and directed by Alphonse Puthren — whose previous film Premam became a cult hit — is set for an Onam season theatrical release. Director Puthren announced on social media that "Gold is melting this Onam," building anticipation for what marks a major Malayalam release for both lead actors.

Why the Kasavu Endures

The Kasavu saree's staying power lies in its democratic appeal. It crosses religious and regional lines — Onam is a secular festival celebrated across Kerala regardless of faith — and its accessibility ranges from handloom cooperatives to high-end designer reinterpretations. For the diaspora, draping a Kasavu during community Onam celebrations in cities from Houston to London serves as a tangible connection to home.

As fashion trends cycle through maximalism and minimalism, the Kasavu's essential character — understated, elegant, rooted in craftsmanship — remains constant. Nayanthara's continued embrace of that simplicity only reinforces the point: some traditions don't need reinvention to remain relevant.
image_caption: Nayanthara poses in a traditional saree, showcasing the minimalist elegance that has made her a style reference for South Indian festivals. The actress is set for an Onam season release with her film Gold alongside Prithviraj Sukumaran.
nri_angle: Kasavu sarees are a staple at diaspora Onam gatherings worldwide, connecting NRI Malayalis to Kerala's cultural identity through fashion.
author: Diaspora Desk
